experiences.name: Grandes Alpes: Lake Geneva to the Tarentaise
experiences.description: The northern leg of the Route des Grandes Alpes, from Thonon on Lake Geneva over Les Gets, the Col des Aravis, the Col des Saisies and the Cormet de Roselend down to Bourg-Saint-Maurice. Four long, rhythmic climbs with lake and glacier scenery. The high passes are closed by snow outside summer, so check opening dates.

experiences.name: Iseran and Galibier
experiences.description: The heart of the Route des Grandes Alpes: from Bourg-Saint-Maurice up to the Col de l'Iseran, the highest paved pass in the Alps, down the Maurienne and over the Télégraphe and Galibier to Briançon. Hairpins, big drops and two of the best-known summits in cycling and touring.

experiences.name: Grandes Alpes: Briançon to Nice
experiences.description: The southern finale of the Route des Grandes Alpes: Izoard, Vars and the Col de la Bonette, then the long Tinée valley and gorges down to the Mediterranean at Nice. The Casse Déserte below the Izoard and the Bonette ring road are the highlights.

experiences.name: Cayolle and the Daluis Gorges
experiences.description: From Barcelonnette over the Col de la Cayolle to Guillaumes, then through the red gorges of Daluis to Puget-Théniers. A quiet high pass followed by a narrow road cut into rust-coloured rock.

experiences.name: Serre-Ponçon Lake to Barcelonnette
experiences.description: From Embrun along the shore of the Lac de Serre-Ponçon, Europe's largest artificial lake, then up the Ubaye valley through its gorges to Barcelonnette. A short, easy ride on tarmac with turquoise water on one side and the first big Alpine peaks ahead; a good warm-up before the high passes.

experiences.name: Route Napoléon
experiences.description: Napoleon's 1815 march from the Riviera to Grenoble, ridden in reverse: Gap, Sisteron, Digne and Castellane on fast, sweeping national roads, then the hills above Grasse down to Cannes. A relaxed, scenic day with long open bends and no big passes.

experiences.name: Vercors to Ventoux
experiences.description: From Grenoble through the Vercors via the Bourne gorges, the Grands Goulets and the tunnels of the Col de Rousset to Die, then south to Mont Ventoux and its summit road. Limestone cliffs, then the lavender country of Provence.

experiences.name: Verdon Rim to Valensole
experiences.description: From Castellane along the northern rim of the Gorges du Verdon past Point Sublime and La Palud to Moustiers-Sainte-Marie, then across the Valensole plateau via Riez to Manosque. A tight canyon road followed by rolling plateau farmland.

experiences.name: Ventoux and the Nesque Gorges
experiences.description: Up Mont Ventoux from Malaucène, across the bare summit to Sault, then down the Gorges de la Nesque to Carpentras. A big climb with a lunar summit and a cliff-edge descent through the gorge.

experiences.name: Luberon Hilltop Villages
experiences.description: A slow ride from Avignon through Gordes, Roussillon, Bonnieux and Lourmarin to Aix-en-Provence. Ochre cliffs, stone villages and market squares, with plenty of reasons to stop.

experiences.name: Monte-Carlo Rally: Turini
experiences.description: From Menton up to Sospel and over the Col de Turini, the mountain stage of the Monte-Carlo Rally, then down the Vésubie valley to Nice. Tight hairpins through fir forest just behind the Riviera coast.

experiences.name: Three Corniches
experiences.description: Nice to Menton on the cliff roads above the sea: Èze, La Turbie and Roquebrune-Cap-Martin, with Monaco below. Short and busy, and best on a weekday morning.

experiences.name: Pyrenees: Tourmalet to Foix
experiences.description: From Lourdes over the Col du Tourmalet and the Col de Peyresourde to Bagnères-de-Luchon, then east on the Menté and Portet d'Aspet roads to Saint-Girons and Foix. A full day of Tour de France climbs and quiet forest passes. Check that the high passes are open.

experiences.name: Basque Country Villages
experiences.description: From Biarritz inland through Espelette, famous for its red peppers, to Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port. Whitewashed villages and green hills with short, easy bends, and a good first taste of the western Pyrenees.

experiences.name: Volcanoes, Puy Mary and Aubrac
experiences.description: A long crossing of the Massif Central: from Clermont-Ferrand through the Monts Dore and the Pas de Peyrol below the Puy Mary, then Saint-Flour and the Aubrac plateau to Laguiole and the Millau viaduct. Empty volcanic roads and wide plateau views.

experiences.name: Tarn Gorges and Cévennes
experiences.description: From Millau up the Gorges du Tarn through La Malène and Sainte-Enimie to Florac, then over the Cévennes ridges to Saint-Jean-du-Gard. Cliffs and stone hamlets in the canyon, then forested mountain roads.

experiences.name: Mont Lozère to Mont Aigoual
experiences.description: From Mende over the granite ridge of Mont Lozère by Le Bleymard and Le Pont-de-Montvert, then across the Cévennes to the weather station on Mont Aigoual. Empty mountain roads, chestnut forest and big open views; the whole ride is on tarmac.

experiences.name: Aigoual to the Cirque de Navacelles
experiences.description: From the summit of Mont Aigoual down through the Cévennes foothills to the Cirque de Navacelles, a meander of the Vis river cut into the Causse du Larzac. Quiet, winding departmental roads all on tarmac, with a spectacular view over the canyon at the end.

experiences.name: Ardèche Gorges
experiences.description: From Aubenas to Vallon-Pont-d'Arc, then the scenic road along the rim of the Gorges de l'Ardèche to Saint-Martin-d'Ardèche and Pont-Saint-Esprit. A string of belvederes over the river canyon.

experiences.name: Cap Corse Coast Road
experiences.description: Round the northern tip of Corsica from Bastia by Macinaggio and Centuri, then down the west coast to the Genoese-tower village of Nonza above its black-pebble beach. A narrow, twisting coast road with sea views the whole way.

experiences.name: Corsica West Coast
experiences.description: From Calvi down the western coast by Galéria, Porto, the red rocks of the Calanques de Piana and Cargèse to Ajaccio. Very narrow corniche roads above the sea with sheer drops. Allow generous time, as the average speed is low.

experiences.name: Alsace Wine Road and Route des Crêtes
experiences.description: From Strasbourg through the wine villages of Obernai and Riquewihr, then south to Guebwiller and up onto the Route des Crêtes, the ridge road that runs past the Col du Markstein and the Hohneck to the Col de la Schlucht, before dropping to Gérardmer. Half-timbered villages in the vineyards, then open ridge roads in the Vosges.

experiences.name: Loire Valley Châteaux
experiences.description: From Orléans through Chambord, Chenonceau, Chinon and Saumur to Angers. Royal châteaux and tufa-stone towns along gentle roads. A culture day with very little twist, so plan the stops.

experiences.name: Dordogne Castles and Cliff Villages
experiences.description: From Sarlat through Beynac, La Roque-Gageac and Domme above the Dordogne river to the cliff-hung pilgrimage town of Rocamadour. Stone villages and castles on easy valley roads.

experiences.name: Mont-Saint-Michel to Étretat
experiences.description: From Mont-Saint-Michel to the D-Day beaches by Sainte-Mère-Église, the Pointe du Hoc and Arromanches, then on to Honfleur and the white cliffs of Étretat. A long day of history and coast on easy, mostly straight roads.

experiences.name: Brittany North Coast
experiences.description: From Saint-Malo west along the Emerald Coast to Erquy, then Paimpol and the pink granite rocks near Perros-Guirec, ending in the ferry port of Roscoff. Cliffs, small harbours and quiet coastal roads.
